description: Given two strings s and t, return the number of distinct subsequences of s which equals t. A subsequence is a string that can be derived from another string by deleting some or no characters without changing the order.
intuition: Think of it as choosing which characters in s to 'highlight' to spell out t. For each character in s, you either use it (if it matches the current character in t) or skip it. The DP counts all ways to make these choices, building up from smaller subproblems.
approach: Use 2D DP where dp[i][j] = number of ways to form t[:j] from s[:i]. If s[i-1] == t[j-1], dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + dp[i-1][j]. Otherwise, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j].
jsWalkthrough:
Input: s = "rabbbit", t = "rabbit"

sLen=7, tLen=6
Initialize: dp[i][0] = 1 for all i (empty t matched 1 way)

Fill DP table row by row (selected key cells):

i=1 (s[0]="r"), j=1 (t[0]="r"): match!
  dp[1][1] = dp[0][1] + dp[0][0] = 0 + 1 = 1

i=2 (s[1]="a"), j=2 (t[1]="a"): match!
  dp[2][2] = dp[1][2] + dp[1][1] = 0 + 1 = 1

i=3 (s[2]="b"), j=3 (t[2]="b"): match!
  dp[3][3] = dp[2][3] + dp[2][2] = 0 + 1 = 1

i=4 (s[3]="b"), j=3 (t[2]="b"): match! (second b)
  dp[4][3] = dp[3][3] + dp[3][2] = 1 + 1 = 2

i=5 (s[4]="b"), j=3 (t[2]="b"): match! (third b)
  dp[5][3] = dp[4][3] + dp[4][2] = 2 + 1 = 3

... continuing fills ...

dp[7][6] = 3

Output: 3 (three ways to choose which "b" to skip)
explanation:
1. dp[i][j] = number of ways to form t[:j] as a subsequence of s[:i].
2. Base case: dp[i][0] = 1 (empty t can be formed from any prefix of s).
3. If characters match, either use s[i-1] (dp[i-1][j-1]) or skip it (dp[i-1][j]).
4. If characters do not match, must skip s[i-1]: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j].
5. Answer is dp[m][n].
hints: For each character in s, you can either include it or skip it.
dp[i][j] depends on whether s[i-1] matches t[j-1].
The base case is that an empty t has exactly one subsequence match.

timeComplexityBreakdown.variables: m = s length; n = t length; both are nonempty in this problem.
timeComplexityBreakdown.note: Every state performs at most one addition from a diagonal state and one copy from the previous row.

complexityVariables.m: Number of characters in the source string s.
complexityVariables.n: Number of characters in the target string t.
